valley_base: Use case: historical-scene. Create the fixed master BACKGROUND of an original historical western strategy game's layered panorama, Hotspring, a fictional semi-arid American frontier valley around 1872. Display as realistic matte painting, wide 16:9 landscape. Camera on hillside, moderately oblique bird's eye, altitude enough to read both buildable sites, cinematic composition with horizon in top 28%. Establish invariant geography for later compositing: weathered low ridges behind valley, a narrow river with willows flowing from center background toward lower left, flat sandy parcel land with sparse scrub on the river's near bank in the lower left to center, drier broad raised ochre terrace on the right with a visible slope from both sites connected by winding faint dirt track. North bank sparse trees, darker low Black Ridge on upper right. Both broad building sites are empty, unoccluded and legible, especially middle and lower third. Dry muted gray sage, clay and dusty ochre, real plants and gritty soil, soft late-afternoon side light from left, no dazzling sunsets. Hotspring does not yet exist: no houses, cabins, tents, wagons, people, signs, roads beyond a faint existing track, structures, overhead utility lines, text, logos or watermark. No identifiable real community. The buildings and people will be layered on this one exact image later. Natural restrained historical painting with clear geographical landmarks, no park or fantasy aesthetic. Single panoramic plate.

Add five worn canvas-covered emigrant wagons, a few tired travelers, horses, and minor dust kicking up as they descend the dirt trail into this exact valley, first wagon prominent near lower right, with a roughly repaired wheel, rope and crates. River visible, faint distant cooking vapor, no buildings or erected camp. Documentary frontier arrivals c.1872. Text and title are added later in the UI; no lettering. Use case historical-scene for original game Les Colons de Hotspring.
